text:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — sustained router fallback loop detected for dedicated pools in us-west1. High latencies and increased 5xxs. Auto-paging to @maria (on-call). Please ack and triage. :rotating_light:

maria: acked. looking at the router dashboards now. seeing a spike in `fallback_count` and most traffic is being sent to `fallback-variant-v1` which is overloaded.

kevin: tagging in — I was on standby. any customer impact visible?

maria: Grafana: us-west1 dedicated pool available_capacity_estimate dropped to negative values around the same time as an influx of traffic. Router reacted by routing to fallback variants in eu-west and us-east which then triggered regional fallbacks. basically a loop.

dylan: that sounds like the metric decorator flip we patched yesterday? Could be the sign inversion in the capacity estimator.

ashley: @maria can you paste the relevant query output?

maria: pasted: ```query: sum(rate(router_fallback_total[1m])) by (pool) -> us-west1 spiked to 450 rps at 13:02 UTC
metric: dedicated_pool_available_capacity_estimate{pool="us-west1"} -> -12.3 at 13:01:57 UTC
logs: router: routing decision: fallback to variant=fallback-variant-v1 reason=capacity_estimate_negative
```

samir: if the estimator goes negative the router treats it as zero and triggers fallback. If fallback nodes are in other regions and they have capacity churn, the smart-routing policy might incorrectly reclassify them as bad too and keep moving traffic.

irene: paging history shows two customer-facing products saw elevated error rates — `search-api-prod` and `chatstream-v2`. Estimated affected requests ~120k in the last 10 min. Need quick mitigation to stop blackholing.

kevin: temporary mitigation idea: flip router policy to prefer local pool if capacity_estimate is within safety window, and disable cross-region fallback for 10m. Also throttle outbound reroutes. I can push a routing policy patch to canary immediately.

maria: +1, do that. Also can we scale the dedicated pool up while we patch the metric? Might buy time.

dylan: scaling request submitted to Dedicated autoscaler: `rb scale-pool --pool us-west1-dedicated --count +4`. Response: queued -> started. ETA 90s.

ops-bot: Autoscaler: accepted scale request id=scale-4829, target_replicas=12, start_time=2026-07-04T13:03:25Z

samir: I'm going to disable the metric decorator that normalizes `available_capacity_estimate` until we fix the sign bug. That should stop negative values flowing into router. Will do config roll to canary now.

ashley: please also enable `fallback_throttle` to 0.1 on routers in us-west1 to slow churn.

maria: rolling config to canary: `curl -XPOST https://config.internal/v1/routers/us-west1/canary -d '{"disable_capacity_normalizer": true, "fallback_throttle": 0.1, "restrict_cross_region_fallback": true}'`

kevin: canary applied to 5 routers. Observing metrics... fallback_count dropping by ~40% on the canary nodes.

dylan: scale finished: replicas=12 -> capacity increased. backend queue drained on scaled nodes.

irene: customer impact: error rates for `chatstream-v2` down from 12% -> 3% in canary shard, still 7% cluster-wide. We should route more traffic to canary as safe.

maria: switching global router to prefer canary control plane for us-west1 for next 5m to accelerate mitigation. Doing gradual shift 10% increments.

samir: config fix confirmed: source of negative values is an uninitialised counter when `gpu_idle` is false, sign flip in estimator. Opening bug: https://tracker.internal/ISSUE-4521

kevin: quick customer comms: ops-team, please prepare an advisory noting intermittent 5xxs in US regions between 13:01-13:20 UTC, root cause under investigation, mitigation in progress.

ashley: will draft.

maria: FYI starting on-call handoff: @kevin, I'm going offline in ~20m. want to handoff active items?

kevin: I got the lead. I'll keep monitoring the routing metrics and the scale. If fallback_count stays low and error rates <1% for 15min, we'll call it mitigated.

dylan: follow-ups: (1) hotfix the metric normalizer and add unit test for sign, (2) add guard in router when capacity_estimate < -1 -> treat as telemetry-bad and consult alternate signals, (3) improve autoscaler visibility so we don't rely on single estimator for scale decisions.

samir: I'll own (1) and (2). tracking ISSUE-4521 and ISSUE-4522.

irene: customer impact count: two top-tier customers hit; SLO alerts triggered. I'll coordinate support tickets and credits if needed.

ops-bot: Incident timeline saved to #incidents with id=INC-2026-0704-01. Postmortem owner required.

maria: thanks team. handing off to @kevin. I'm leaving notes in the incident doc and will be available on pager if needed. :v:

kevin: acknowledged. continuing watch. will escalate back to full war room if we see any regression.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> monitoring. P1 -> mitigated=false. Next update in 10m or on change.
